title: His aunt's dances and early bands in Tremé
summary: His father's oldest sister gave dances at Economy Hall and other halls, hiring Manuel Perez, Kid Rena and Punch. As a boy he ran errands for her.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Do you remember any of the parades or any other early bands or dance artisers when you were a kid?

Oh yes, in fact I remember practically, I should remember all of them because my aunt, her name, it's Kalis Dele, she was my father's oldest sister. She gave dances continuously. Oh, where did they give those dances? She used to give at the economy hall, at the cooperatives hall, the Jeanne Zami and the Franz Zami. She gave them many dances. Most of the old timers remember, but in those days, well I was a kid, although interested in music. Did you hear the music? Did you hear the dances too? Yes, yes, yes. You got to go there. Yes, you know we couldn't naturally dance or anything, but we were there. They took us to everything. So, Maria Perez used to play for us sometime. And in fact she had Kit René a lot, she had Punch, had Buddy Pt, to play for a different time. In fact I used to go give the guys, I mean not give, but I mean she used to send me to give me a receipt and I'd bring it to her. Of course she used to send me all over when I was a kid, you know, and I was always interested in music.
Mother's dances, and they weren't the organization, they gave it just the private party.
